correctness.rationale: The unattenuated monodromy is X^T X for X=exp(τ B), B=[[0,p],[q,0]], with determinant one. Using B²=pq I gives trace 2+4κ²sinh²(aτ); dividing the leading log multiplier by the full period 2τ gives the proposed exponent. H(u)=asinh(κ sinh u) has H''(u)=κ(1−κ²)sinh(u)/(1+κ²sinh²(u))^(3/2), so H(u)/u is strictly decreasing for κ>1. Its distinct endpoint limits give the strict finite-duration sign cases, including equalities at the limiting recovery rates; equal rates instead give a constant exponent. The small-u cubic coefficient is −κ(κ²−1)/6, and H(u)=u+log κ+O(exp(−2u)), giving both claimed root asymptotics at fixed unequal rates. An independent direct matrix-product calculation and bisection reproduced the worked example to floating-point rounding; it did not rerun the source script or independently exhaust its test suite.
residual_risks: This is an equal-phase two-dimensional local stability theorem. The computation is finite and does not establish nonlinear behavior at criticality or outcomes beyond the stated model.
